clue.text: My boss used up oxygen in brain, struggling to be charming

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' sends the word upwards, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: the setter's boss on a newspaper is the editor, abbreviated ED

indicators.note: the oxygen symbol is placed inside the word brain
the letters struggle out of their order and are rearranged

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A setter's editor, gasping for breath, tries hard to seem charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used up' turns ED into DE; O put 'in' BRAIN gives BROAIN, which 'struggling' rearranges to BONAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a suave, confident and charming manner, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Ship involved in exercises over here!

indicators.note: the ship abbreviation is wrapped inside the letters for exercises

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercises
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A sailor calls out during a shipboard workout to attract someone's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark belongs to the definition: the answer is a whispered call for attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections used to catch someone's attention quietly, a call saying come over here.

clue.text: Breakfast in bed?

definitions.meaning: a smoked herring, a traditional British breakfast dish
a person having a kip, that is sleeping, is one in bed

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a smoked fish eaten at breakfast and, playfully, one who kips or sleeps.

clue.text: Elementary thing, the boast of a heavy drinker?

definitions.meaning: a form of a chemical element with a different number of neutrons

definitions.text: the boast of a heavy drinker?
definitions.meaning: split into three words it reads '...', to tope meaning to drink heavily

explanation.surface: A drunk brags about some simple matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I SO TOPE: a toper is a heavy drinker, so a toper might boast 'I so tope!'
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry deals with elements, and each variant atom of an element counts as an elementary thing.

clue.text: River bridges very old, in truth

indicators.note: the river's name spans across the other pieces like a bridge

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river famous for its bridges
so as in 'so good' means very

explanation.surface: A Scottish river crossed by ancient bridges, the clue claims honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forth, in Scotland, is famous for its rail and road bridges, which makes 'bridges' a well-hidden container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation meaning indeed or truly, used to stress a statement's sincerity.

clue.text: Meaningless talk of point between rings penetrates so, after levitation

indicators.note: the group of rings and point pushes into the middle of the other word
levitated in a down clue, the word rises and so reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: such as in 'it was so cold' and 'such cold'

indicators.note: the point sits between the two rings

parts.note: each O is a ring shape
a cusp is a pointed end, where two curves meet

explanation.surface: A magician's patter about rings and points before a levitation trick.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'after levitation' means read upwards, giving HCUS; 'penetrates' pushes the ringed point in after the H. The surface pretends to be a stage magician's act, apt for a conjuror's chant.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjuror's chant has come to mean nonsense or deceptive jargon, meaningless talk.

clue.text: Accent afoot?

definitions.meaning: a strong regional, especially Irish, way of speaking
a sturdy shoe with perforated decoration, so it is on a foot

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an Irish or Scottish accent and a stout leather shoe worn on the foot.

clue.text: See 23
Setter almost back on the Guardian's scent

indicators.note: the shortened word for the setter is turned back to front
the dog loses its last letter, nearly all of it

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog
the clue appears in the Guardian, so its own paper's is 'our'

explanation.surface: The setter almost returns to pick up the Guardian's trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims DOG to DO, and 'back' turns that to OD. A setter is both a crossword compiler and a gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour and scent are synonyms, both meaning a smell.

clue.text: Political item sees party doing U-turn between two of its leaders?

parts.note: Michael Foot led the Labour Party in the early 1980s

indicators.note: a U-turn sends the party's short name back the way it came

parts.note: Lab is the usual short form of the Labour Party
L is the leading letter of the word Labour

explanation.surface: A political issue: a party performing a policy U-turn caught between two of its leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led Britain's Labour Party (1980-83); the second 'leader' is the leading letter of Labour. This is also the first half of the theme word, a sport, completed at 24 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A political football is an issue kicked between parties for advantage, so it is a political item.

clue.text: 10 24 down's police once maintaining rights, but wrong, by the way

indicators.note: the old police word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Peelers were early British police, named after Sir Robert Peel

indicators.note: the letters are put wrongly, rearranged

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Old-time police upholding rights, though wrongly, along the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes ITTSBURGH, which with the street goes inside after the first letter. Peelers, after Robert Peel, were Victorian London police. Like the other long lights, this names a team in the theme sport of 10 24.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pittsburgh Steelers are an American football team, one of the sport's clubs.

clue.text: Look for winger

definitions.meaning: to take a ... is to have a look
a male goose, a winged bird

explanation.definitionFit: Gander means both a quick look and a male goose, a bird with wings.

clue.text: One's simple bed's ending — with pillow here?

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word bed is used

parts.note: a pillow is placed under your head in bed

explanation.surface: Someone simple-minded at the foot of the bed, wondering where the pillow goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as D plus UNDER HEAD: where the pillow goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunderhead is a stupid person, so one who is simple.

clue.text: Actor's supporter must be more punctual?

definitions.meaning: the theatre worker who feeds forgotten lines to actors
prompt means on time, so this comparative is more on time

explanation.surface: A stage helper should be the most punctual one in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre prompter supports actors with forgotten lines; also the comparative of prompt, punctual.

clue.text: See 22 down
As region volatile, get map out

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and changeable, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: Since the area is unstable, get a map out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is a link word; the definition is 'map out', meaning plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To map out a plan is to arrange or organise its parts, so the phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: 10 24 down's hip, a mouth and other organs

parts.note: hip and chic both mean stylish
gob is British slang for mouth
ears are organs other than the mouth

explanation.surface: Someone stylish, with a mouth and further body parts.
explanation.walkthrough: GOB is everyday British slang for the mouth. The definition names a team of the sport at 10 24.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chicago Bears are an American football team, one of the sport's clubs.

clue.text: Glitter obscures death list

indicators.note: the singer's name covers the loss, hiding it inside

parts.note: Gary Glitter was a British glam-rock singer
a death is a loss

explanation.surface: Sparkle hides a list of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glitter' is the surname of Gary Glitter, a 1970s British glam-rock singer, so the clue gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of terms with their meanings, an alphabetical list.

clue.text: Red newt filling roll

indicators.note: the young newt is stuffed inside the roll like a sandwich filling

parts.note: a roll is a list, as a roll of names
an eft is a young newt

explanation.surface: A newt is the filling in a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' is the definition, a left-winger, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A Red is a communist or socialist, and so a left-winger.

clue.text: Coax ecstasy past first of guards, going through wearing mask

indicators.note: the ecstasy letter comes past, after, the rest

parts.note: to be in clothes is to be wearing them

indicators.note: the G passes through into the veil

parts.note: a veil masks the face

indicators.note: only the leading letter of guards is taken

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Getting ecstasy past the guards by wearing a mask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going through' sets G inside VEIL to make VEIGL; 'past' puts E after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle is to coax or wheedle someone into doing something by flattery.

clue.text: Desire to hold underwear up close

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole thing is read upwards, backwards
the yearning word holds the garment inside it

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire
a bra is underwear

explanation.surface: Wanting to hold up one's underwear tightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' gives YBRAEN, and 'up' turns it round because this is a down clue, read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby and close both mean at a short distance.

clue.text: Tyrant making point about further perception

indicators.note: the point goes round about the perception letters

parts.note: a dot is a point
ESP is extrasensory perception, sensing beyond the usual senses

explanation.surface: A dictator claims to have psychic powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'further perception' is perception beyond the senses: extrasensory perception.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who uses power cruelly, a tyrant.

clue.text: 10 24's got something to do, say, in corrupt business, company in dire straits for starters

indicators.note: the pieces sit in the opening letters of the words that follow
only the first letters of dire and straits are used
the part of speech goes inside the company name

parts.note: Enron was the US energy company that collapsed in a fraud scandal
a verb is a doing word, as 'to do' is

explanation.surface: A team gets involved in a crooked business while its company is in dire straits.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' makes ENVERBRON; the second 'in' places that and the company between the starts of 'dire straits'. Enron was a US energy firm that collapsed in 2001 amid fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: The Denver Broncos are an American football team, one of the sport's clubs.

clue.text: 10 24 down's debatable answers kind about religion embracing godhead

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the other pieces
debatable answers are open to question, so their letters are rearranged
the religion embraces the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Shinto is the native religion of Japan
the head, first letter, of god

explanation.surface: Disputed answers of a kind relating to a religion holding a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'debatable' makes WANREDSKINS, and 'about' wraps it round the religion holding G, splitting after its second letter. The team now plays under another name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Washington Redskins were an American football team, one of the sport's clubs.

clue.text: Sculpture's gone to the wall

definitions.meaning: an idiom for having failed financially, gone bankrupt

explanation.surface: A statue has been ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust means both a head-and-shoulders sculpture and broke or bankrupt, gone to the wall.
